title: Introduction: Why AI Product Launches Don't End at Launch
text: Hello, I'm Vineet Kumar Sayrawat. Launching an AI product is not one day. It is a staged path from a small pilot to full production, and the work continues after launch. Here is how product managers run it. An AI launch keeps going long after launch. Models drift, users surprise you, and providers change their models. The real work is the monitoring, learning, and improving that follows. Here is the path: pilot, beta, A/B testing, staged rollout, monitoring, customer feedback, and continuous improvement. Each stage

title: The Staged Path: Pilots, Betas & Clear Exit Criteria
text: Lowers risk before the next one raises exposure. Start with a pilot, a small group, often internal or friendly customers with close support. Learn whether the product solves the problem at all. Then widen to a beta with real users. Set clear exit criteria in advance, for example, quality scores, error rates, and satisfaction, so the decision is not a feeling. Use A/B testing to compare the new AI experience against the current one on the metrics that matter. Then roll out in stages, a few percent of traffic, then more, using feature flags. Watch the numbers at each step and keep a rollback ready, so you can switch back quickly if something breaks. After launch, monitoring is the product. Track production metrics, answer quality

title: A/B Testing & Staged Rollouts with Rollback Triggers
text: Samples, error and fallback rates, latency, cost per request, and safety incidents. Add alerts for sudden changes. Review real conversations regularly with privacy rules, because dashboards miss problems that people can see. Customer feedback closes the loop. Add thumbs and comments, and read support tickets. Turn failures into new test cases. Also, plan for model changes. A provider update or your own upgrade can shift behavior, so rerun your evaluation set and roll the change out gradually, just like a feature. Then improve continuously. Review metrics weekly. Fix the biggest failure first.

title: Production Monitoring: Tracking Quality, Latency & Costs
text: Grow the test set from real problems. Revisit cost and model choice as prices fall, and tell users what improved, because trust grows when people see you listening. So, launching.
